rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: an imperative lecture heading blurs the mood switch that lets a declarative exercise heading register as a law. Chunk 5's new header (L35) "Keep your context where it loads optimally" is imperative-mood, unlike the file's other four headers ("Rules have a ceiling", "Prohibitions stop; taste steers" — declarative claims). Checked the maintainer block for an accept-note before flagging, per the hard-boundaries instruction: raw L47 names this exact title as a maintainer call — "The lecture closes on *Keep your context where it loads optimally* (Antti-directed 2026-08-23; reordered to last the same day so the live return is the final thing seen...)" — the heading's wording and closing placement were both authored by the maintainer, not generation drift. Scored PASS on that basis rather than REVISE; the residual tension (§15 doesn't yet name a carve-out for this shape) is filed below as a rule question, not held against the file.
